tests.title: Boxes: borders, radius, shadows, outline, opacity, overflow clipping
tests.hint: Each box should look like the reference picture posted next to this message.

tests.title: Colours and gradients: linear, radial, conic; named, hex, rgb() and hsl() colours; colour functions out (hwb, lab, oklch, color(), color-mix); background images
tests.hint: Each box should look like the reference picture posted next to this message.

tests.title: Text (1/2): system font families, weights, decoration, alignment
tests.hint: Fonts differ between platforms: compare the structure (which line is bold, where text breaks, what is underlined), not the exact letter shapes.

tests.title: Text (2/2): ellipsis, RTL and Arabic shaping, emoji; line clamp and text-shadow out
tests.hint: Fonts differ between platforms: compare the structure (which line is bold, where text breaks, what is underlined), not the exact letter shapes.

tests.title: Layout: flex with gap, grid, table, positioning and z-index, float; multi-column out
tests.hint: Each box should look like the reference picture posted next to this message.

tests.title: Transforms and effects (1/2): 2D transforms; 3D transforms out (must look flat); filter blur, brightness, drop-shadow
tests.hint: Each box should look like the reference picture posted next to this message. The 3D row must look flat.

tests.title: Transforms and effects (2/2): backdrop-filter blur/brightness; other filters, blend modes, clip-path and mask out
tests.hint: Each box should look like the reference picture posted next to this message.

tests.title: CSS animations and transitions, live: slide, spin, pulse, steps, a frozen frame, a transition on tap
tests.hint: Moving rows: the box should move as the caption says (the picture shows the frames it moves between). Frozen row: must match exactly. Tap the last box once.

tests.title: Web Animations (element.animate, pause and seek, keyframe offsets, control of CSS animations)
tests.hint: Top row moves; the other rows are frozen by script and must match the picture exactly. Tap the bouncing ball to stop it half-way.

tests.title: Canvas 2D (1/2): shapes and paths, line styles, colours, gradients, text, alpha
tests.hint: Each canvas should look like the reference picture posted next to this message.

tests.title: Canvas 2D (2/2): transforms and clipping; shadows, ctx.filter, conic gradients and patterns out; a chart
tests.hint: Each canvas should look like the reference picture posted next to this message.

tests.title: Inline SVG (1/2): shapes, structure and viewBox, gradients, text
tests.hint: Each picture should look like the reference picture posted next to this message.

tests.title: Inline SVG (2/2): CSS on SVG; clipPath/mask, filters and SMIL out
tests.hint: Each picture should look like the reference picture posted next to this message. Nothing moves: SMIL is out.

tests.title: Images: data: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP; object-fit; background images; SVG images, BMP/ICO and remote URLs out (placeholder)
tests.hint: Each row should look like the reference picture posted next to this message.

tests.title: Taps, pressed state, details, drag, hover (desktop), link opening with confirmation
tests.hint: Do what each row says; the widget shows ✓ when it saw the input.

tests.title: Theme: light-dark(), prefers-color-scheme and onTheme follow the chat theme live; the --tg-theme-* palette
tests.hint: Switch the chat between light and dark: the live box must match the picture for the current theme.

tests.title: Out of the profile, neutralised the same way everywhere: form controls, inner scrolling, sticky, named fonts, 3D, popover over the chat
tests.hint: Each box must look like the reference picture: the out-of-profile feature is simply not there. The popover is dropped: its red box is an ordinary block in the bubble, shown from the start. Tap “Show popover”: nothing changes, and nothing may appear outside this bubble.

tests.title: Unstyled document: the renderer's defaults for the root and the text (no CSS at all)
tests.hint: Compare with the picture for the chat's theme: the bubble's own colour behind the text, the chat's text size, the same spacing, a table with row lines, the button in the client's style. Change the chat text size: the text follows.

tests.title: A body background without a margin reset fills the whole bubble (root background propagation)
tests.hint: The whole bubble is dark blue, edge to edge: no strip of the bubble's own colour around the text, in either theme.

tests.title: Text selection: nothing is selectable by default; user-select: text makes a paragraph selectable, its children included
tests.hint: Select text the way your client selects message text (on a phone through the bubble's menu, with a mouse by dragging): only the blue-bordered paragraph can be selected, the bold word in it too, and copying gives its text.

tests.title: The client's time over the bottom corner of a widget with no caption below it: the widget keeps clear of it with env(safe-area-inset-bottom) and --tg-content-safe-area-corner-*
tests.hint: No caption below this widget (none, or one above it): the time with its ticks sits over the bottom right corner (bottom left in a right-to-left interface) on a dark backing, inside the lighter corner box. The blue footer reaches the bubble's bottom edge; its last line runs beside the time, never under it. A tap on the time does nothing in the widget.

tests.title: openLink: the confirmation shows the full URL
tests.hint: Tap each button. Each time the client asks first and shows the whole URL (path, query; the IDN host in its xn-- form), then opens the browser.
tests.expect: A native confirmation with the full URL and Open / Cancel; Open goes to the browser (or the in-app browser, as the client usually does).

tests.title: openTelegramLink: t.me links open inside the client
tests.hint: Tap each button: the link opens inside Telegram (a channel, a post, a user), never in a browser.
tests.expect: The client's own t.me handling, with its usual confirmations; no external browser.

tests.title: Invalid links and links over 256 characters are rejected
tests.hint: Tap Try all: no dialog may appear for the bad links; then tap the 256-character link: that one asks.

checks.name: a 256-character URL is accepted (the client asks)

tests.expect: No dialog for a non-https URL, user info, javascript:, tg:, a t.me URL through openLink or a 257-character URL (the widget gets a TypeError); a dialog for the 256-character one.

tests.title: Links need a press: a timer cannot open one, one press opens one link
tests.hint: Tap the first button and wait 2 s: nothing opens. Tap the second: exactly one dialog, not two.
tests.expect: No dialog from the timer (the host drops it as activation-blocked); one dialog for the two calls of one press.

tests.title: Haptics: every impact style, notification type and selection
tests.hint: On a phone tap each button: each one is felt, and they feel different. Desktop and web: nothing happens, no error.
tests.expect: impact light/medium/heavy/rigid/soft, notification error/success/warning, selection played with the platform's generators; nothing on desktop and web.

tests.title: Haptics rate limit: a burst of 5, then 10 per second
tests.hint: On a phone: Burst asks for 20 at once, you feel 5. Stream asks for 100 over 2 s, you feel about 25. Hidden: tap, scroll the bubble away within a second, nothing is felt.
tests.expect: A bucket of 5 refilled at 10 per second; the rest dropped silently; nothing from a hidden widget.

tests.title: Storage survives the widget being dropped and re-created
tests.hint: Tap +1 three times. Scroll far up the chat until the bubble is rebuilt (Started goes up), scroll back: both counters are still 3.
tests.expect: localStorage and sessionStorage come back with the re-created widget (the client passes its copy at creation).

tests.title: localStorage survives an app restart, sessionStorage does not
tests.hint: Tap +1 twice. Quit the app completely and open this chat again: local is still 2, session is 0.
tests.expect: localStorage is on disk per (account, chat, message); sessionStorage is in memory until the app restarts.

tests.title: Storage is deleted with the message
tests.hint: Tap Fill (about 15 KB). Delete this message: the client's widget-storage debug listing (or its storage stats) no longer has an entry for it. The same after Clear cache.
tests.expect: Both areas are deleted with the message, with the chat or its history, with the account and on Clear cache.

tests.title: QuotaExceededError at 4 KB
tests.hint: Tap Fill: it writes 1 KB values until the client refuses; the line must say QuotaExceededError at 4 KB, for local and for session.
tests.expect: 4096 bytes of keys and values per area; the refused setItem throws a DOMException named QuotaExceededError and stores nothing.

tests.title: After 2 crashes in a row the widget stays stopped
tests.hint: Tap Crash: the frame freezes with the Widget stopped badge. Scroll away and back: it starts again (Started 2). Crash again, scroll away and back: it stays stopped with the badge.
tests.expect: The frozen last frame with the localised badge; one rebuild after the first crash; none after the second, until the app restarts (the HTML never changes, so no edit brings it back).

tests.title: Who gets a press: double taps always, holds and horizontal drags by touch-action, vertical drags never, and the edge strip
tests.hint: Blue (touch-action: none): drag the knob sideways, hold “Hold me” (it counts the time); no swipe-to-reply, no menu, the counters move. Drag up or down over blue: the chat scrolls, “to the chat” counts it. Striped (auto): long press = the message menu, swipe = reply; “cancelled” counts each one. Double-tap anywhere in the widget: no reaction, the widget counts the double taps. Bottom pad: a drag from the red strip is the back gesture, from the rest it moves the green mark.
tests.expect: A double tap over the widget is always the widget's: both clicks and dblclick, on every element, and the client's reaction stays on the bubble outside the widget. A vertical drag is always the chat's: the list scrolls and the widget gets pointercancel, on touch-action: none too (v0.1.3). touch-action: none gives the widget horizontal drags (on both axes once a drag started sideways) and holds (it gets contextmenu, no message menu); on auto the bubble takes holds and swipes and the widget gets pointercancel; a press in the leading 20 px of the widget is never the widget's (system back). The client follows the shared gesture policy (gesture-policy.ts: 500 ms hold, 300 ms / 40 px double tap, 10 px slop, 20 px edge strip).

tests.title: Taller than the cap: a hard clip
tests.hint: The widget is 3000 px tall. The bubble shows the top 600 px and cuts it: no scrolling inside, no expand or fullscreen button. The last mark you see is the cap.
tests.expect: The bubble's height is the cap, 600 px on every client (the shared v0.1.0 value; maximumHeight / maxHeightDp / the web MAX_HEIGHT); content below is clipped.

tests.title: Theme palette: themeParams and --tg-theme-* follow the chat live
tests.hint: Each row: the swatch from themeParams and the one from the CSS variable are the same colour and match the chat. Switch the theme or night mode: all rows change at once, the counter goes up.
tests.expect: Every themeParams key as #rrggbb, the same values as --tg-theme-* on the root, updated in one task with themeChanged.

tests.title: A forwarded copy has its own storage
tests.hint: Tap +1 three times, then forward this message to another chat: the copy shows 0, the original still 3. +1 on the copy does not change the original.
tests.expect: Storage keyed by (account, chat, message id): the destination chat's copy starts empty.

tests.title: The bot edits the widget's state: the widget changes without a restart
tests.hint: Tap Ask the bot to edit a few times. Each time both values go up by one, chatDataChanged and publicDataChanged each count one more, Started stays 1, and the answer line says edited N.
tests.expect: The bot's editMessageWidgetData reaches the running widget (updateMessageWidgetData, then setData): chatDataChanged, then publicDataChanged, in one task; no restart, the HTML never changes; the answer carries no state.

tests.title: The bubble takes the bot's size anchors before load, then the content height
tests.hint: The bot sends this widget four times: width 0 + height 0 (the default placeholder, then the content height, 240 px), width 0 + height 300 (a fixed 300 px bubble that stays 300 after load), width 300 + height 0 (a 300 px wide widget, then its content height), and width 300 + height 300 (fixed both). The cached height is used next time the auto bubbles scroll in.
tests.expect: Width 0 = the bubble's width, W = a fixed width clamped to [200, max]; height 0 = auto (placeholder, then the reported 240 clamped to [50, 600], cached per message), H = a fixed clamp(H, 50, 600) that the content does not change.

tests.title: The resize anchor: the edge the widget chose stays put when its height changes
tests.hint: Anchor bottom (the start): tap + line a few times: the buttons stay under your finger, the bubble grows upward and the messages above it move up; − line shrinks it back the same way. Tap the anchor button for top: now + line keeps the bubble's top still and pushes the buttons and the messages below down. Try both with the bubble near the top and near the bottom of the screen.
tests.expect: With every height the host reports the widget's anchor (setResizeAnchor, v0.1.3); the chat list keeps that edge of the bubble in place on screen: bottom, the content above moves and the bubble's bottom edge does not; top (the default), the content below moves. No jump of the anchored edge while the height animates. A bubble off screen keeps what is on screen in place.

tests.title: A request on a tap gets the bot's answer
tests.hint: Tap Ping: “sending…”, then the bot's answer “pong, <your first name>”; the client shows nothing of its own. Tap Two at once: the first is answered, the second fails at once with BUSY.
tests.expect: messages.getBotWidgetQueryAnswer per tap with the widget's data; its result goes back to the widget (no toast, alert or link from the client); one request in flight per widget.

tests.title: A forward asks the bot only if the widget was sent with fwd_allow_queries
tests.hint: The bot sends this twice: “live forward” (fwd_allow_queries) and “plain forward”. Forward both to another chat. In the forwards: Ask on the live one is answered; on the plain one it says NOT_ALLOWED. Neither shows chatData or a chat type; only the live one shows a viewer (your name).
tests.expect: A copy gets is_copy; can_query only for a fwd_allow_queries widget, taps only. The client passes the flags from the media; the widget of a copy gets no chatData and no chatType, and the viewer only with can_query; the bot gets only from, data and widget_id.

tests.title: The network marker: shown exactly where a tap may send data to the bot
tests.hint: The bot sends this twice. On “allow_queries” the client shows its network marker; on “no queries” it shows none. Forward both: neither forward has a marker (no fwd_allow_queries). Tap the marker: the client explains it (a tap may send data to the bot's server).
tests.expect: The marker exactly where the message has can_query (context.canQuery): never without allow_queries, never on a forward of a widget without fwd_allow_queries, never on a preview.

tests.title: copyText: the client copies on a tap and shows what it copied
tests.hint: Tap Copy: the client's toast shows CONF-2026-OK, and that is what you paste. Tap Copy later: nothing is copied a second later (no tap). Tap Copy twice: one tap, one toast.
tests.expect: copyText on a tap: copy the text and show a toast with the text itself (truncated if long); outside a tap nothing (activation-blocked); one copy per tap. The widget is not told.

tests.title: A preview in the inline results: the widget's data, no input, nothing about the user
tests.hint: In any chat type the test bot's username and conf-preview. In the list the widget says Preview yes and shows its state; a tap on it selects the result: Taps stays 0. Send it: the message says Preview no, shows a viewer, and Tap me counts.
tests.expect: A widget result in the inline list (botInlineMessageWidget) runs with context.preview and the result's data: no input routed to the widget, no requests or actions, no viewer, no storage, no network marker; the sent message is a new widget.

tests.title: watchPublicData: the client polls a shared widget's state while the widget watches
tests.hint: Tap Start: for two minutes the bot changes the shared state every 10 s (editWidgetData with cache_time 5, nothing pushed). Watching: the value follows within about 5 s. Tap Unwatch: it stops following; Watch: it catches up at the next poll. Scrolled off screen nothing is polled.
tests.expect: The client polls getWidgetPublicData only while the widget watches (onWatchPublicData / watchesPublicData) and is on screen, one carrier per widget_id, at the object's period; a new value reaches the widget as publicDataChanged.

tests.title: A group: one chat state for all members, drawn per viewer
tests.hint: The bot sends this into the test group. Each member taps +1: everyone sees the same count and who tapped last (one chat state for the group), and each sees their own name under You. Nobody's widget asks without a tap.
tests.expect: In a group chatData is one value for all members, edited by the bot (updateMessageWidgetData; in a supergroup with the channel's pts); requests on a tap only; viewer is each member.

tests.title: Haptics without a touch: one second, then nothing for nine (a widget cannot buzz the phone)
tests.hint: Tap Start, then do not touch the widget: 6 s later it asks for a haptic every 50 ms for 15 s (the counter runs). You feel one second of them, nothing for nine, one more second, then nothing. Then hold Hold and buzz for a second and lift your finger: it asks every 100 ms while you hold and for 8 s after; you feel it while you hold and about 6 s after (the 5 s after a touch, then one series), then nothing.
tests.expect: Outside a touch the first haptic opens a 1 s series; the next series needs a touch or 10 s since the last began (one series after a touch at any time later). During a touch (a press on the widget and 5 s after it is lifted) haptics pass under the rate limit (a burst of 5, then 10 per second).
